prerequisites: It is recommended to have knowledge of differential and integral calculus of single-variable functions, differential calculus of multi-variable functions, and vector spaces. These contents are included in the Algebra and Calculus courses taught during the first semester of the first year.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering related to: complex variable, integral calculus in several variables and differential equations.
Basic knowledge of computer programs with application in engineering.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, which enables students to learn new methods and technologies, as well as providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Industrial Technical Engineer's activity.
Formulate and calculate integrals of functions of two and three variables and apply them to solving engineering problems.
Parameterize curves and surfaces with ease, perform the integration of scalar and vector functions over them, and apply it to solving engineering problems.
Know the basic properties of complex functions and be able to approximate them through series expansions.
Understand the essential qualitative aspects of differential equations: existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions.
Acquire proficiency in the explicit resolution of first-order and higher-order differential equations and relate the latter to first-order systems.
Understand the concept of partial differential equations.

teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (computer room, software for calculations)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.15*NL + 0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, where NL is the laboratory practices grade, NA is the classroom practices grade, and NC is the average of two written partial controls. If a student does not achieve a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 in NC, the final grade will be the minimum between NF and 4. For extraordinary calls, NF = 0.15*NL + max{0.15*NA + 0.7*NC_exam, 0.85*NC_exam}, where NC_exam is the single exam grade; a minimum of 4 in NC_exam is also required, otherwise the final grade is min(NF, 4). Students requesting differentiated evaluation will be assessed by a theoretical exam (85%) and a practical exam (15%).
